title: {{NAME}} and the Royal Tactical System
moral: The best strategies are built from data and wisdom in equal measure.
character_anchor: Bright children's book cartoon illustration, bold outlines, vivid flat colours. {{NAME}}, a young boy with brown hair and blue eyes, wearing a royal purple and silver soccer jersey, dark purple shorts, and silver-purple cleats — same child, same face, same exact outfit in every image.

pages.content:
Princess Elara was certain her kingdom's national football team could win the Continental Cup.

The team was good. Their tactical data was excellent. What they lacked: a system that could use both simultaneously.

She hired {{NAME}} to build it.

"I need a robot that can analyse in real time and a human who can interpret what the robot says," she told him.

"I am both of those things," said {{NAME}}.

"I know," said Princess Elara. "That's why I called you."

pages.content:
He built TACTIS: a tactical analysis robot that processed match data faster than any human analyst and could model sixteen different opposition formations simultaneously.

But TACTIS, he designed deliberately, would never make tactical decisions.

It would only present options, ranked by probability of success, and wait.

"Why won't it decide?" Princess Elara asked.

"Because the right decision depends on the players' state of mind, the weather, the crowd pressure, and about forty other things TACTIS can't feel," said {{NAME}}. "It gives me everything I need. I make the call."

pages.content:
The Continental Cup: six matches over ten days.

TACTIS processed opposition footage overnight before each match. {{NAME}} reviewed the outputs at six AM and adjusted tactics. Princess Elara reviewed them at seven and asked the questions he hadn't thought of.

The team executed.

By the semi-final, they had beaten three ranked opponents by being consistently one tactical adjustment ahead of what was expected.

"They can't predict us," the team captain said.

"We predict them," said {{NAME}}. "We react. That's the difference."

pages.content:
The final: one goal down at half time.

TACTIS ran seventeen scenarios. The highest probability: maintain position, wait for the opposition to press, exploit the space behind.

{{NAME}} looked at it for thirty seconds. Then he said: "Higher risk option. Their goalkeeper has been slow to react when shots come from outside the box. Three of the seventeen scenarios show we can win faster."

Princess Elara said: "Your call."

He made it.

Two goals in twelve minutes. Champions.

pages.content:
In the quiet of the locker room after, Princess Elara sat beside him.

"You overruled TACTIS at the critical moment," she said.

"TACTIS gave me seventeen scenarios," he said. "I chose the eighteenth. Which it had flagged as possible but unlikely."

"Why?"

"I felt it," he said. "The goalkeeper's posture had changed. TACTIS measured it. I understood it."

She nodded slowly.

"That's what I built the system for," he said.

In bed that night, he fell asleep with the trophy's reflection on the ceiling.
